blocks.text: Catalogs reference external public streams and accept your own reachable URLs. Formats, audio, subtitles and rewind windows depend on the source and platform. Native apps do not automatically load the media bundled with Pages.

items: Confirm playback with a VOD preset. To compare audio, subtitles or quality, use a source containing the required tracks or renditions.
Open Screen and controls for your platform and retain the original values. Edits are drafts. Before applying, check whether the action reloads the source or recreates the Player.
Check the picture, controls, events and applied code after Apply. To undo an applied change, enter the original values and apply again. Reset discards draft edits; it does not undo a completed Apply.

blocks.text: Basic forms cover source, playback and UI settings; SDK inspectors use each SDK’s types. Names, application timing and numeric limits differ by SDK. Check these platform-specific areas:

items: Common fields: HTTP/HTTPS URL and format, title, poster, start position and reference. Buffer settings use seconds; bitrate caps use bit/s. Follow each platform’s meaning of blank and default values.
Apple: StyleConfig.scalingMode for video scaling, and initial audio/subtitle preferences using public track-selection APIs.
Android: player-wide and source-specific audio priorities, external WebVTT subtitles and HTTP retry delays.
React Native and Vega: external WebVTT URL, label and language. React Native default-track metadata differs from Vega’s enable-on-load setting.

blocks.text: Invalid input leaves applied settings unchanged. Android reloads or recreates on a valid Apply even when values are unchanged; Apple, React Native and Vega do so only after a change. Follow each platform’s Screen and controls for draft reset and override removal.

Initial track preferences differ from selection during playback. Android and React Native default-track metadata does not enable subtitles; select them in the subtitle menu. Vega displays enabled external WebVTT as plain text. Follow the Apple guide for initial selection and native HLS subtitle conditions.

blocks.text: Allow your application identifier on the Player license. The Web SDK’s localhost exception does not apply to native apps. Analytics also requires permission for that identifier on its license. Update permissions when changing an identifier. Normal native playback does not need an account API key.

blocks.text: Use the pinned Node.js and pnpm versions and create the root .env from .env.example. Follow Local setup and licenses for shared configuration. The placeholder below leaves optional Analytics collection disabled; run the preparation commands from the repository root.

blocks.title: Run from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
bash scripts/sync-env.sh
pnpm --filter @showcase/ui-shared build
pnpm sync:webui

sync-env.sh creates ignored license files for Apple, Android and React Native. Vega needs its separate SDK and runtime:config and is not handled by sync-env.sh. Follow each platform’s README and implementation guide to generate and build, then use Screen and controls. Never commit license values.

blocks.text: DVR is the available live rewind window. These apps use 0 for the live edge and negative values for the past. −30s seeks to 30 seconds behind the live edge, rather than 30 seconds before the current position. The SDK-reported range limits the requested position.

rows: On-demand video with a known finite duration
Classified as live, with an available rewind window and the sample’s DVR setting enabled
The rewind window is unavailable, not yet known, or disabled in the sample
Length of the rewind window reported by the SDK
By default, within 1 second of the live edge

blocks.text: HLS may report a zero rewind window just after startup; play and wait for the range. Increasing the forward buffer does not extend the stream’s historical media. The live edge moves during a seek, and request acceptance, SDK completion and display updates occur at different times.

blocks.title: What Allow DVR controls
blocks.text: Allow DVR controls the app’s state calculation and helper rewind buttons. It does not change all seek controls, including the shared UI seek bar, or the SDK’s global DVR setting. Toggling it does not move playback; use Live edge or Go to live edge to return to live. Apple and Android expose a separate SDK time-shifting setting in their player editors.
